newsitem.title: USA: FCC denies Telquest, TCI satellite TV bid.
newsitem.headline: FCC denies Telquest, TCI satellite TV bid.

text.p: The Federal Communications Commission said Tuesday it denied a bid by Telquest Ventures and Tele-Communications Inc to beam TV programs across the United States from a Canadian orbital satellite slot.
The two U.S. companies planned to use two satellites that had not yet been licensed by Canada and that would be owned and operated by a Canadian corporation, Telesat Canada.
The FCC said its policy is to dismiss such applications for direct broadcast satellite (DBS) when a company's satellites have not yet been licensed.

It added that the policy "avoids wasteful and potentially unnecessary staff review of systems that may never provide service and deters applicants from filing such premature applications in an attempt to influence foreign satellite licensing decisions."
In July, the FCC dismissed a similar application from the two companies, citing similar reasons. The two companies then filed an emergency petition with the FCC in August.

During the summer, the Clinton administration had urged the FCC to defer action on the requests because they "raised foreign trade or competition policy issues within the jurisdiction of the Executive Branch."

MCI Communications Corp and Rupert Murdoch's News Corp had been among those calling on the FCC to reject the application. MCI earlier this year paid $683 million at an FCC auction for the last oribtal slot over the United States that allows a company to beam TV signals coast to coast. News Corp has teamed up with MCI to provide a nationwide DBS service.

TelQuest and TCI had argued in their new petition that the Canadian government had provided sufficient authorization for Telesat's proposed satellites in the form of the "support in principle" of John Manley, Canadia's minister of industry.
Manley had spelled out the "support in principle" in a letter, along with the conditions that had to be satisfied before the satellites would be authorized by his government.
The FCC said TelQuest and TCI could refile their applications once the satellites are licensed by the Canadian government.
